name: The New Year
label: Touch and Go
lede: When Bedhead ended, Matt and Bubba Kadane kept the three guitars, kept Steve Albini, changed the name and spread the band across four cities.

hero.by: Matt Kadane with the New Year, June 2007. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Bedhead with a new name on the door
eras.text: Bedhead broke up in 1998 with its members in three different places and a Dallas hair-product company using the same name. Within a year the Kadane brothers were writing again, meaning it as a two-man project, and friends kept getting pulled in until it was a band.

years.h: The Kadanes start over, and four friends sign on
years.p: Matt Kadane in Boston and Bubba Kadane in Dallas add [[Mike Donofrio|dfdc0317-c840-4d56-85fa-9a279ac8e0de]] of Saturnine on bass, [[Codeine|cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58]] and Come drummer [[Chris Brokaw|a05544f2-9341-4c9d-8ba0-7621a23012c6]], and Dallas guitarist [[Peter Schmidt|273a53b1-3052-4749-b10b-e1826b7b1d74]], a part-time Bedhead player.
years.xp:
After Bedhead, Matt Kadane told Deathrockstar, the brothers dropped the idea of another band, then decided they wanted to record again and needed people to play it live. Every one of the others was a friend first: "We would be friends with every one of these guys if we didn't play with them."

The name came from Bubba, who saw it in print and liked how it looked. Schmidt had played in Three on a Hill, Funland and the Legendary Crystal Chandelier.

years.h: Steve Albini again, this time in Chicago
years.p: The band records its first album with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], who had made Bedhead's last record, Transaction de Novo. The line-up wasn't finished yet, so Schmidt is credited on a record he doesn't play on.
years.xp: Kadane described what they wanted from Albini: drums that sound like the room, guitars that sound like guitars, and vocals sitting inside the mix instead of on top of it.

years.h: Newness Ends lands on Touch and Go
years.p: Bedhead's label, Trance Syndicate, had shut down, and the Kadanes already knew people at Touch and Go. Critics heard Bedhead, and the brothers didn't argue.
years.xp: In interviews at the time the Kadanes said the only real difference between Bedhead and the New Year was the name, and that a Bedhead follow-up would have sounded a lot like Newness Ends.

years.p: The brothers write the score for the documentary Hell House. The film is out in 2001; the soundtrack waits until 2004.

eras.title: The band filmed its first video
eras.text: Members drifted off to other projects between records: Brokaw played with Evan Dando and made solo albums, Schmidt finished the last Legendary Crystal Chandelier album. In 2003 they regrouped in Chicago, and Albini was waiting again.

years.h: Josh McKay of Macha makes it six
years.p: The Athens, Georgia musician joins for a stretch in 2003 on keyboards, guitar and whatever percussion is lying around, as the band regroups to record.

yt: 'The End's Not Near', Touch and Go Records
years.h: The End Is Near, and a single that says otherwise
years.p: Albini engineers again. 'The End's Not Near' becomes the band's best-known song, and the Kadanes shoot their first music video, for 'Disease'.
Ben Bridwell's band records its own version of the New Year's best-known song, released on Warner Bros.

eras.title: A history professor goes on a three-month tour
eras.text: By now Matt Kadane taught history in upstate New York and Bubba ran a CD and DVD manufacturing company in Dallas. For the third album they cleared their calendars, wrote around the piano Matt grew up on, and booked the longest tour they'd ever done.

years.src: D Magazine · Wikipedia: The New Year
years.h: Half of The New Year is built on piano
years.p: The self-titled third album keeps the three guitars but brings Matt Kadane's piano forward. AllMusic gives it 4.5 stars; Pitchfork, 7.5.
years.xp:
Matt was an assistant professor of history at Hobart and William Smith Colleges with a sabbatical already planned; Bubba had stepped back from ACME Manufacturing, the company he started in 1997. Bubba told D Magazine he'd "never felt more like going all-out on a record."

Touch and Go's press release said the ten songs dealt with lost time, frustrated desire and the need for other people.

years.cap: The New Year at Locomotiv, Bologna, November 18, 2008
yt: 'Seven Days and Seven Nights' live on Radio Citta del Capo, Bologna, 2008
years.p: [[Will Johnson|9e455882-2bb2-47fa-b1ce-f8516123649d]] joins the US leg of the autumn tour, the start of a friendship that turns into a band four years later.

eras.title: Nine years between records
eras.text: The fourth album started in Chicago in 2012 and then sat. The brothers made a record with friends in the meantime, and when the New Year's album finally came out it was on a different label.

years.h: Brokaw: back in Chicago with "Mr. Steve Albini"
years.p: Brokaw posts that work on a new LP has begun, again with Albini at the controls.

years.h: The Kadanes start Overseas with David Bazan and Will Johnson
years.p: A side band with [[Pedro the Lion|2f360fd9-6440-4896-9f45-8156e8b0b204]]'s [[David Bazan|d1714baa-2174-4233-8272-f537bfa9fbba]] and Centro-matic's Johnson. Its one album arrives June 11, 2013.

years.src: Aquarium Drunkard · Wikipedia: The New Year
years.h: Snow comes out on Undertow, not Touch and Go
years.p: The first New Year album in nine years, released through the Undertow Music Collective with videos for 'Myths', 'Snow', 'The Last Fall' and 'The Beast'.
years.xp:
The delay wasn't the plan. "We expected to put the record out a long time ago," Matt Kadane told Aquarium Drunkard. They'd gone in to record a few songs years earlier, sure the rest would follow quickly.

By then Matt lived in New York and taught history, and Bubba was in Texas scoring film and television.
